newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Commodities marked by new rally in US coffee.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Commodities marked by new rally in US coffee.

text.p: An explosive rally in US coffee prices was reignited on Thursday in panicky trading amid concerns about tight prompt supplies.
"The situation is explosive. Nobody dare sell the market," said one New York trader. "It's a bull market. You can't go against the wind."
The benchmark July New York futures for arabica coffee powered to a new contract high at $2.21 per pound, up around five percent on the day.

Although certified US coffee inventories have risen in the latest daily data, by 565 (60 kilo) bags, this was only the first rise since March 31 and traders said there was still concern about meagre stocks.

More price gains were likely with funds, speculators and roasters (processors) seen set to buy. Traders said overnight comments by brokerage Merrill Lynch that the coming Colombian crop could be delayed could have set the tone for the latest rally.
London futures for the robusta type of coffee, which is in more generous supply, failed to match US gains. By the close, July London robusta futures stood $41 up at $1,659 a tonne.
Many market participants expect tight supplies and the onset of the Brazilian winter to keep coffee buoyant in the coming months.

Smaller-than-expected harvests in many Latin American countries -- most notably second-largest producer Colombia -- and the prospect of a disappointing crop in top grower Brazil in the 1997/98 season may underpin prices, they said.
The Colombian harvest could total less than 10 million bags this crop year, traders add.
Benchmark Chicago wheat futures eased on profit-taking with rain forecast for portions of the drier US Great Plains and signs of showers in key European wheat areas also mentioned, traders said.
These weather patterns suggested potential relief for the crop in drier area of the US and in France.
July Chicago Board of Trade wheat was down five cents at $4.28-1/2 per bushel by the mid-session there.
Gold firmed but within a range, crude oil was little changed and London Metal Exchange copper and aluminium drifted lower.

LME turnover was light due to the May Day holiday in much of Europe and the Golden Week celebrations in Japan. Britain observes a holiday on Monday, May 5, so LME activity is likely to be muted on Friday as well.
A small group of miners at Chile's huge Escondida mine were on strike, as were workers at Quebrada Blanca, another Chilean mine, underpinning copper.
